props.text: Quiet headlands, warm seas, and the Camí de Cavalls.
From April through June and September through November, the island’s ancient 185-kilometer bridal path blooms with wild rosemary, sea fennel and golden afternoon light.
Direct trailhead gate access
Step directly onto Stage 3 and Stage 17 of the historic Camí de Cavalls coastal path from our garden gates.
22°C sea swims into November
Mediterranean water holds summer warmth well into late autumn while the coves remain completely unhurried.
Wood-burning hearths & hydronic floors
Cooler evenings are met with stacked olive firewood, wool throws and radiant limestone floors.

props.text: Before you make plans
Practical answers for an unhurried stay.
Need advice on ferry crossings from Barcelona with your own car, crib setup for young children or chartering our wooden llaüt boat? Ask our host team directly.
More travel & stay logistics

items.a: Dune House sleeps up to six across three bedrooms (two king suites and one twin room) and suits families or friends who want expansive terrace dining above the sea. Blue Shutter Cottage sleeps four in the village of Fornells where you can walk everywhere. Sa Caleta Casita is designed for a couple seeking quiet seclusion among olive trees.
items.q: Which home is best suited for our group size and pace?

items.a: Send us your preferred home, target dates and group size through our stay inquiry form. Host founder Mateu Serra replies within 24 hours with confirmed availability, an itemized seasonal quote including local ecotax, and a direct reservation agreement with zero third-party platform fees.
items.q: How do direct reservations and seasonal availability work?

items.a: All three homes are between 20 and 28 minutes by car from Mahón Airport (MAH). While Blue Shutter Cottage sits right in Fornells village with bus and boat connections, we recommend a compact rental car for exploring hidden north- and south-shore trailheads.
items.q: Do we need a car on Menorca, and how far are the homes from Mahón Airport?

items.a: Every stay includes washed Belgian flax bed linens, Turkish beach towels, straw market baskets, insulated cove coolers, cedar kayaks or paddleboards, and an arrival pantry of estate olive oil, local wine, Mahón cheese, orchard fruit and crusty bread.

props.text: Intimate Hideaway · Sant Lluís Olive Grove
Sa Caleta Limestone Casita: a walled dry-stone sanctuary for two.
Rebuilt from a nineteenth-century orchard keeper’s shelter, Sa Caleta Casita sits behind dry-stone walls among two acres of wild olive, almond and fig trees on the island’s sunny south shore.
Courtyard saltwater plunge & copper shower
Step from the vaulted bedroom directly into a private walled courtyard with a spring-fed limestone plunge basin.
10-minute footpath to Binibèquer & Alcaufar coves
Follow a shaded dry-stone lane down to flat limestone swimming ledges and a quiet cliffside chiringuito.
Off-grid solar & wood-burning limestone hearth
Complete tranquility year-round with underfloor heating for autumn walkers and thick stone walls that stay cool all August.

Residence 01 · Es Grau Biosphere Headland · Sleeps 6
Dune House: for long terrace lunches and open sea horizons.

Perched above the pine-fringed dunes of Es Grau on Menorca’s northeastern nature reserve, Dune House wraps three vaulted limestone bedrooms around a sixty-foot sea-facing terrace and shaded outdoor dining loggia.

props.alt: Limestone dining terrace overlooking coastal dunes and the Mediterranean sea in morning light

props.text: Sleeping Capacity
Up to 6 guests · 2 king suites + 1 twin bedroom
Indoor & Outdoor Area
210 m² interior · 140 m² limestone terrace & loggia
Water Access
4-minute private boardwalk path to Es Grau shallow bay
Nightly Tariff
€240 Low · €285 Mid · €340 High (4-night min)
The best room is outside
Morning light over the water, afternoon shade beneath the sabina beams.

At Dune House, the terrace sets the cadence of the day. Breakfast runs late around the ten-foot chestnut table, afternoon swims end at the warm copper garden shower, and evenings gather around the wood-fired stone plancha as fishing boats cross the horizon toward Illa d’en Colom.
Three sea-breeze bedrooms with cobalt shutters
Every bedroom opens directly onto a stone terrace with louvered Menorcan shutters that lock in the night breeze while filtering morning glare.
Indoor & outdoor cooks’ kitchens
Inside: a monolithic limestone island, Smeg range and espresso grinder. Outside: a shaded stone sink, wood-charcoal grill and herb beds.
Two cedar sea kayaks at the dune gate
Paddle fifteen minutes across calm turquoise shallows to the uninhabited coves of Illa d’en Colom.

Blue Shutter Cottage: village mornings and quiet afternoons behind cobalt shutters.

Tucked along a pedestrian limestone lane in the northern fishing village of Fornells, this restored 1890 cottage pairs whitewashed vaulted rooms with a private bougainvillea-draped breakfast courtyard.

Leave the shutters open
Walk for morning bread, return to a cool limewashed living room.

Blue Shutter Cottage was restored for guests who love the rhythm of a Mediterranean harbor village. Stroll down to the quay at 8:00 for pastries and fresh figs, take the coastal path out toward Cap de Cavalleria, and spend the warm afternoon hours reading beside the courtyard citrus basin.
Walled bougainvillea & citrus courtyard
High limewashed garden walls enclose a private dining patio shaded by a mature lemon tree and trailing crimson bougainvillea.
Original mares-stone vaults & terracotta tile
Hand-scraped beams and reclaimed handmade floor tiles stay naturally cool under bare feet after the beach.

props.text: The Coast · Menorca Biosphere Reserve
A coastline of quiet calas, dry-stone walls, and working harbors.
Protected as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1993, Menorca has resisted high-rise development in favor of ancient stone bridal paths, pine-sheltered coves and family farms.
Every Salt House guest receives our printed coastal notebook with wind-direction cove recommendations, bakery hours and private llaüt boat charter contacts.
Choose your coastal home
Plan your island arrival

props.alt: Mediterranean limestone cove with clear turquoise water and a stone house among pine trees

props.text: An island day, unhurried
Three moments between the pine paths and the harbor quay.
You never need an itinerary here—only a sense of which way the wind is blowing and when the village bakery pulls its morning trays from the oven.

props.alt: Quiet turquoise Mediterranean limestone cove in early morning sunlight with wooden kayak

props.text: Morning · North & East Headlands
Start on foot along the Camí de Cavalls.

Follow the dry-stone trail from Es Grau over the headland to Cala Tortuga and the whitewashed Favaritx lighthouse. The water is clearest before nine, when ospreys circle the cliffs and the cove sand is untouched.
Midday · Beneath the Wild Olives
Leave three hours for lunch in the shade.

Pick up heirloom tomatoes, capers, sobrasada and crusty country bread from the Alaior farm stand, or walk down to a stone harbor cellar for grilled squid and chilled white wine while the afternoon heat passes.

props.alt: Shaded outdoor lunch table beneath an olive tree overlooking the coast
Traditional wooden Menorcan llaüt boats moored in a calm stone fishing harbor at golden hour

props.text: Golden Hour · Fornells Bay & Cavalleria
Set out by wooden llaüt before sunset.

Our skipper Pau Cardona keeps a restored 32-foot wooden Menorcan llaüt moored in Fornells harbor exclusively for Salt House guests—dropping anchor in red-rock coves that can only be reached cleanly by sea.
Island field guide
Coves, markets, and distances from each residence.
Because Menorca is only 48 kilometers from east to west, swapping between the wild ochre north shore and the pine-fringed turquoise south shore takes less than half an hour.
